originality.rationale: Original full text yields only epsilon<1/kappa for Hermitian SPD, whereas this theorem proves and attains the larger universal threshold 2 sqrt(kappa)/(kappa+1) for exactly the same sketched harmonic pencil. Relevant harmonic/ordinary Ritz sources and semantic database findings were compared by hypotheses and implication, not solely by titles. Classical acute-angle bounds are credited; unresolved older equivalent-angle formulations remain a documented risk.
residual_risks: An earlier paper on accretive oblique projections, angle distortion of SPD operators, or generalized harmonic Ritz pencils could encode the same sharp threshold without the same terminology; no exhaustive historical uniqueness is claimed.
The extremal deterministic sketch does not assert that a specific common random-sketch distribution realizes the bad event with positive probability at a stated finite sample size.
The theorem does not extend to general nonnormal positive-real matrices, floating-point computed pencils, or all convergence hypotheses of the restarted method.

value.rationale: Section 5.3 of a 2026 matrix-function Krylov paper singles out right-half-plane harmonic Ritz values as a nontransparent convergence assumption. This theorem resolves the complete deterministic Hermitian-SPD distortion frontier, changes sufficient embedding accuracy from 1/kappa to asymptotically 2/sqrt(kappa), and proves tightness at both singular and negative endpoints. The precise quantity directly governs whether the reduced harmonic pencil is well-defined and has the required spectral location, independent of trial dimension. The claim is mathematical but does not advertise a full restart convergence theorem or distributional sketch probability.
